domain_entities.name: LeaveRequest
domain_entities.purpose: Represents an employee's request for leave of a specific type, tracking its full lifecycle from draft through approval/rejection to cancellation.

domain_entities.name: LeaveBalance
domain_entities.purpose: Tracks an employee's leave entitlement, usage, and remaining balance for a specific leave policy within a fiscal year.

domain_entities.name: LeavePolicy
domain_entities.purpose: Defines the rules and entitlements for a specific category of leave (annual, sick, emergency, etc.), including accrual behavior, notice requirements, and approval mandates.

domain_entities.name: LeaveType
domain_entities.purpose: Enumeration of leave categories. Each type maps to a LeavePolicy that governs its rules. The feature explicitly requires annual, sick, and emergency; unpaid, maternity, and paternity are defined for completeness.

domain_entities.name: Employee
domain_entities.purpose: Represents an employee in the organization. Used for leave request ownership, manager approval chains, and balance tracking.

domain_entities.name: AuditLog
domain_entities.purpose: Immutable record of all state-changing operations on leave entities, fulfilling GP-002 audit requirements.

modules.name: shared-types
owns: LeaveType enum (annual, sick, emergency, unpaid, maternity, paternity)
LeaveRequestStatus enum (DRAFT, SUBMITTED, APPROVED, REJECTED, CANCELLED)

recommended_phases.title: Phase 1: Shared types and foundation modules
recommended_phases.rationale: Establish shared-types (all enums, DTOs) and the employee module — these have zero internal dependencies and are required by everything else. Also set up the audit module since it's a cross-cutting concern mandated by GP-002.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 2: Policy and balance domain modules
recommended_phases.rationale: Build policy (leave rules, max days per type) and balance (per-employee leave balances, deduct/restore). Both depend only on shared-types; policy is also a dependency of balance. These are the core domain logic modules.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 3: Leave application module
recommended_phases.rationale: Build the leave module — the orchestrator that wires employee, policy, balance, audit, and notification together. This is the largest module: models, repository, service, controller, and routes. Depends on all prior phases.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 4: Notification module and integration wiring
recommended_phases.rationale: Build the notification module (email/in-app notifications for leave events). Wire up the Fastify plugin registration, RBAC guards on routes, and end-to-end integration tests.

architecture_md_update:
## Leave Management Module

### Overview
The leave management module enables employees to apply for annual, sick, and emergency leave, managers to approve or reject requests, and the system to track leave balances. It is implemented as a modular monolith within the existing Fastify/TypeScript/PostgreSQL stack, adhering to all GOLDEN_PRINCIPLES (audit, RBAC, transaction semantics).

### Domain Entities
- **LeaveRequest** — core entity representing an employee's leave application. Lifecycle: DRAFT → SUBMITTED → APPROVED/REJECTED; can be CANCELLED from DRAFT, SUBMITTED, or APPROVED.
- **LeaveBalance** — per-employee, per-policy, per-fiscal-year tracking of entitlement, used, and remaining days. Lifecycle: ACTIVE, EXHAUSTED, FROZEN, CLOSED.
- **LeavePolicy** — defines rules for a leave type (annual, sick, emergency, etc.): entitlement, accrual, notice period, manager approval requirement. Lifecycle: ACTIVE, INACTIVE.
- **LeaveType** — enumeration: annual, sick, emergency, unpaid, maternity, paternity.
- **Employee** — existing employee entity (from HR context) used for requester and manager relationships.
- **AuditLog** — immutable record of all state-changing operations (GP-002).

### Business Rules
- **BR-001 (Balance Sufficiency):** Before a LeaveRequest transitions from DRAFT to SUBMITTED, the system verifies that the employee's LeaveBalance for the corresponding LeavePolicy has `remainingDays >= requested days`. If insufficient, submission is rejected.
- **BR-002 (Manager Approval):** If the LeavePolicy has `requiresManagerApproval = true`, only the employee's designated manager (Employee.managerId) with the manager role may approve or reject. If `false`, the request auto-approves on submission.

### Module Structure
```
src/
  shared/types/          # LeaveType, LeaveRequestStatus, BalanceStatus, DTOs
  modules/
    employee/            # Employee model, repository, service
    policy/              # LeavePolicy model, repository, service
    balance/             # LeaveBalance model, repository, service
    leave/               # LeaveRequest model, repository, service, controller, routes
    audit/               # AuditLog model, repository, service
    notification/        # Notification service (email/in-app)
```

### Dependencies
- `leave` depends on all other modules (employee, policy, balance, audit, notification) and `shared-types`.
- `balance` depends on `policy` and `shared-types`.
- `policy`, `employee`, `audit`, `notification` depend only on `shared-types`.
- No circular dependencies; dependencies flow inward.

### Data Model (Conceptual)
- **employees** — existing table; used for employee and manager references.
- **leave_policies** — defines leave types and rules. Indexed by `leave_type` and `is_active`.
- **leave_requests** — core transactional table. FK to employees (employee_id, approved_by) and leave_policies. Indexed for employee self-service, manager queues, overlap detection, and audit.
- **leave_balances** — tracks entitlement per employee/policy/fiscal year. Compound index on `(employee_id, fiscal_year)` for the most frequent query.
- **audit_logs** — cross-cutting audit trail. Compound index on `(entity_type, entity_id)` for entity history.

### API Endpoints (Fastify Routes)
All endpoints enforce RBAC (GP-005) and validate inputs (GP-003).
- `POST /leave/requests` — submit a new leave request (employee).
- `GET /leave/requests` — list own requests (employee) or pending for manager (manager).
- `GET /leave/requests/:id` — get request details.
- `PATCH /leave/requests/:id/approve` — approve (manager).
- `PATCH /leave/requests/:id/reject` — reject (manager).
- `PATCH /leave/requests/:id/cancel` — cancel (employee).
- `GET /leave/balances` — get own balances (employee).
- `GET /leave/policies` — list active policies.

### Integration Points
- **Audit (GP-002):** Every state change in LeaveService calls `IAuditService.record()`.
- **Notification:** LeaveService calls `INotificationService` on submission, approval/rejection, and cancellation.
- **Employee Service:** Used to resolve manager relationships and validate employment status.
- **Balance Service:** Deducts on approval, restores on cancellation of an approved request.

### Phase Recommendations
1. Shared types and employee/audit foundation.
2. Policy and balance domain modules.
3. Leave application module (orchestration).
4. Notification module and final integration wiring.

This design extends the existing architecture without contradiction, following the modular-monolith style with clear boundaries and inward dependency flow.
sql_schemas: table employees | fields: id, employee_number, first_name, last_name, email, manager_id, department, hire_date, termination_date, employment_status, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: manager_id -> employees.id | indexes: employee_number: unique lookup by employee number for HR operations; email: unique lookup for authentication and contact resolution; manager_id: team-level queries — list direct reports for manager approval workflows; department: filtering employees by department for org-chart and reporting views; employment_status: filtering active/inactive/terminated employees for eligibility checks

table leave_policies | fields: id, policy_name, leave_type, entitlement_days, accrual_rate, max_accumulation, minimum_notice_days, requires_manager_approval, is_active, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | indexes: leave_type: filtering policies by leave type when resolving applicable policy for a request; is_active: filtering active policies for eligibility and balance calculations

table leave_requests | fields: id, employee_id, leave_policy_id, start_date, end_date, reason, status, approved_by, approved_at, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; leave_policy_id -> leave_policies.id; approved_by -> employees.id | indexes: employee_id: list all leave requests for an employee (self-service dashboard); status: filter requests by status for manager approval queues and HR reports; leave_policy_id: join to policy for entitlement validation; start_date, end_date: date-range queries for calendar views and overlap detection; approved_by: lookup requests approved by a specific manager for audit trails; employee_id + status: compound access pattern — employee filtering their requests by status

table leave_balances | fields: id, employee_id, leave_policy_id, total_entitlement, used_days, remaining_days, fiscal_year, status, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; leave_policy_id -> leave_policies.id | indexes: employee_id: look up balances for an employee's self-service view; employee_id + fiscal_year: compound access — employee's balance for a specific year (most common query); leave_policy_id: join to policy for entitlement rules; fiscal_year: filtering balances by fiscal year for accrual and reset operations

table audit_logs | fields: id, entity_type, entity_id, action, old_values, new_values, performed_by, performed_at, ip_address, user_agent, created_at | pk: id | indexes: entity_type + entity_id: compound lookup — all audit records for a specific entity instance (e.g., a leave request's full history); performed_by: filter audit trail by actor for compliance reviews; performed_at: time-range queries for audit reports; action: filter by action type (APPROVE, REJECT, etc.) for workflow analytics
